newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 3.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Bertie Ahern, leader of Ireland's main opposition Fianna Fail party, has ruled out doing a deal with Sinn Fein if Friday's election leads to a hung parliament.
- Belfast has elected its first ever nationalist lord mayor.
- The Royal Ulster Constabulary is questioning 15 people in connection with the killing of an off-duty RUC officer at the weekend.
- The chairmen of Northern Ireland's multi-party talks, due to resume at Stormont, appealed for all sides to seize the opportunity for progress provided by the election of a new British government.
- The number of Irish women having abortions in Britain has reached a new high.
- A group of Northern Ireland business organisatons has warned of the economic risks of another summer of sectarian parades, riots and community violence.
- Ireland's central bank may be set for a confrontation with the Department of Finance, according to Bloxham stockbrokers economist Alan McQuaid.
- Intel Ireland is seeking planning permission for a major expansion of its plant in Leixlip.
- Further contacts between Irish government officials and Sinn Fein were hanging in the balance following the discovery of an Irish Republican Army (IRA) landmine in West Belfast.
- Agriculture minister Ivan Yates is pressing the Egyptian authorities to confirm a date for restarting imports of live cattle from Ireland.
